subject: Integration accelerator: SDK handoff, endpoint migration plan, and retry/timeout guidance
body:

Subject: Integration accelerator: SDK handoff, endpoint migration plan, and retry/timeout guidance

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the meeting this morning. Per our mutual action plan, I'm starting the formal handoff to our implementation team so we can get you into sandbox and plan the endpoint migration window. Attached is a first-draft integration spec and a zip with sample SDK snippets for Node/Python.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm which SDK language your engineers want to use (node/python/java).
- Share a preferred 2-week cutover window for the endpoint migration (we've penciled Dec 7–20).
- Any existing rate-limit policies or traffic shaping we should know about.

What I'll coordinate from Redwood:
- Implementation lead: Monica Patel will be primary contact for engineering handoff and sample verification.
- Sandbox credentials and test dataset by end of day Thursday.
- A short runbook for retries/timeouts and recommended defaults attached.

Attachments: integration_spec_v1.pdf, sample_snippets.zip, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to the rollout.

Thanks Rachel — this looks great. Quick answers:
- We'll use Node for the SDK (backend team prefers JS runtime).
- Dec 10–14 is our preferred migration window (low traffic week).
- Current gateway imposes a soft rate limit of 300 reqs/min per API key; we can temporarily raise that for the cutover if needed.

Question from our eng lead: what are your recommended retry/backoff defaults for transient 429/503s? Also, do you have guidance for KV cache warmup (we often see a flurry of cache misses after cutover).

Jordan
Director of Integrations, Clearline Health

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@clearlinehealth.com>, Priya Suresh <priya@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration accelerator: SDK handoff, endpoint migration plan, and retry/timeout guidance

Jordan — hi, Monica from Redwood's implementation team. Short version: we have a conservative default that suits most customers and a migration-friendly variant. See below.

Recommended defaults (SDK layer):
- Idempotency: add a request-id header (X-Request-ID) for all write/commit operations.
- Retries for 429/502/503: up to 4 attempts (1 initial + 3 retries).
- Backoff: jittered exponential backoff with base 300ms, multiplier 2.0 (i.e., delays ~300ms, 600ms, 1.2s). Add full jitter (random between 0 and delay) to avoid thundering herd.
- Timeout: per-request network timeout: 10s; token-streaming operations: 30s socket timeout but close and resume logic at 60s.
- Circuit breaker: open after 10 consecutive 5xx/connection failures, reset after 30s.
- Rate-limit handling: on 429 we recommend honoring Retry-After header when present; otherwise apply backoff above.

KV cache warmup during cutover:
- Strategy A (recommended for cutover): Gradual ramp — send a set of warmup requests that mirror typical session prefixes over a 12–24 hour period prior to migration + small synthetic traffic for low-frequency prefixes. We can provide a warmup script (small Python tool) to push representative traffic into cache.
- Strategy B: aggressive seeding — for initial hour after cutover expect higher latency; run a focused seeding job for top 200 prefixes.

I've attached a short snippet (from sample_snippets.zip) below for Node showing retry/backoff scaffold.

--- code ---
const defaultBackoff = (attempt) => Math.min(1200, 300 * Math.pow(2, attempt)); // ms
async function callWithRetries(fn) {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < 4) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (err) {
      if (!isTransient(err) || attempt === 3) throw err;
      const delay = Math.random() * defaultBackoff(attempt);
      await sleep(delay);
      attempt++;
    }
  }
}
--- end code ---

I'll drop the warmup script and a short runbook into the Drive link and can run warmup with your engineers during the Dec 8–10 prep window if you'd like.

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Thanks Monica — that all looks sensible. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- For streaming calls we'll need the socket timeout guidance specifically. You mentioned 30s; what is the best practice to resume partial streams?
- Can your warmup script simulate different user prefixes and also replay a small historical trace (we can provide a 24-hour sample trace).

Also, the engineering lead asked if Redwood supports per-route quotas in Dedicated mode (we plan to use dedicated capacity for JP region later).

Priya
Lead SRE, Clearline Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Suresh <priya@clearlinehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration accelerator: SDK handoff, endpoint migration plan, and retry/timeout guidance

Priya / team — small replies inline: 

- Streaming resume: our SDK exposes a resume token in the stream metadata. Best practice: on socket interruption, attempt to reconnect and send a resume request with last-acknowledged token. If the token is expired (older than 5m in default config) the stream will fall back to a short reconnect-and-snapshot pattern; you'll see higher TTFB but correctness is preserved. We'll include example code in sample_snippets.zip under node/streaming_resume.js.

- Warmup script: yes — we can accept a 24-hour sample trace and parameterize the warmup script to replay user prefixes with adjustable QPS. Monica will coordinate offline to validate the trace format.

- Per-route quotas in Dedicated: short answer yes — Dedicated supports per-route quotas and token-level cost tracking; we'll loop in the product team if you want default quota templates for JP. Karthik, can you flag a person from Product to scope templates?

Next steps:
1) Jordan / Priya: confirm Node SDK and migration window (Dec 10–14).
2) Clearline: upload 24-hour sample trace to the Drive link by Mon, Nov 30.
3) Redwood: Monica will drop warmup script and schedule a 30-min run with Clearline SREs on Dec 8 at 11:00 PT.

I'll update the mutual_action_plan.xlsx with these items. Thanks all.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com



(Attachments referenced: integration_spec_v1.pdf (integration checklist + endpoints), sample_snippets.zip (node/python examples including streaming_resume.js), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (milestones and owner list)).
